transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I guess what brought me in is… things got weird at work. I’m a waitress, and during service I started freezing up, like I couldn’t keep moving. Or I’d do things completely out of order. One time I was just standing by the soda station holding the cash drawer key, repeating table numbers instead of closing checks. It scared people, and honestly it scared me too.
During one of these episodes, were you fully aware of your surroundings and able to remember what happened afterward, or did you lose consciousness or have a gap in your memory?

I don’t think I passed out or anything like that. I was… aware enough to know I was at work, and I remember parts of it afterward. But it’s not always clear, like some of it feels blurry because I was so stuck and confused in the moment.
During these episodes, have you or anyone else noticed any involuntary movements, like lip-smacking, chewing motions, jerking, or a fixed stare, happening while you're 'stuck'?

I don’t think anyone mentioned lip-smacking or jerking. What they noticed was more that I’d just freeze in the middle of service, or I’d start doing things in the wrong order. Like I’d be standing by the soda station holding the cash drawer key and repeating table numbers instead of closing out checks. That was the part that scared people.
When one of these episodes happens, about how long does it typically last from start to finish?
I’m not really sure exactly. It feels like a few minutes, maybe, but I haven’t timed it. Sometimes it seems short after the fact, but while it’s happening it feels longer because I’m so stuck.
During these episodes, or at other times, have you heard voices, seen things others don't, or had thoughts or beliefs that others found strange or unfounded?

Yeah… I have heard things sometimes. Like when I’m closing at work, or even at home in the kitchen, I’ll hear a woman’s voice say my name or tell me I’m doing the count wrong. It sounds clear enough that I’ll answer back, and then I realize nobody else heard it.
How long has this been going on overall—when did you first start noticing these freezing episodes and hearing the voice, and has it been continuous or getting worse over time?

It’s been about a year and two months altogether. I first started noticing the freezing and the voice around the time they asked me to take on the evening shift lead responsibilities. It wasn’t all at once, but it’s kind of been building since then.
Do you have any medical conditions—like a seizure disorder, thyroid problems, or a past head injury—or do you use alcohol or recreational drugs, that might be related to these episodes?
I’m not sure. I don’t have anything like that that I know of. I don’t really use drugs, and I don’t think there’s a medical thing I can point to. I guess I’m not sure what would count, though.

Aside from the voice and the freezing episodes, have you noticed any unusual beliefs—like feeling that people are watching you, plotting against you, or that your thoughts are being controlled or read by others?

Yeah… I have had that. I keep feeling like a couple of the servers, and this one regular customer, are watching how I ring things in. Like they’re checking for mistakes or trying to catch me doing something wrong.

And sometimes I’ll see little things on the tickets, like marks or changes, and it feels like they’re leaving signs to prove they’re trying to get me fired. My husband says it’s just normal restaurant mix-ups, but it doesn’t really feel that way to me when it’s happening.
Do you continue to hear that voice or have these suspicious feelings about coworkers even when you're not having one of the freezing episodes, or do they only happen during those episodes?

It’s not only during the freezing. The suspicious feelings can be there at other times too, especially at work. I’ll be ringing things in and feel like a couple of the servers, or that regular customer, are watching me and leaving little signs on the tickets to show they’re trying to get me fired. My husband says it’s probably just normal restaurant mess-ups, but in the moment it feels like more than that.
Since these experiences began, have you noticed a change in your ability to keep up with work, relationships, or daily self-care compared to before?

Yeah, definitely. Work has gotten harder. I’m making more mistakes and getting confused during service and closing, and it’s started causing problems for everyone. I was supposed to maybe get a shift-lead opportunity, but now I feel like I’m close to losing that because I can’t keep things straight.

At home, too… my husband says I’m barely present with him anymore. Like I’m there, but not really with him. I don’t mean to be that way, but it’s changed.

During this past year, have you also had stretches of time with significant changes in your mood—like feeling very depressed, hopeless, or low energy, or the opposite, unusually elevated, irritable, or full of energy—that happened along with or separate from these voices and freezing episodes?

I’m not really sure. I mean, I get stressed and worn out, especially with everything going on at work, but I haven’t noticed a clear stretch where my mood was really different like that.

I don’t think I’ve had times where I was unusually energized or on top of the world. And I wouldn’t say I’ve been deeply depressed for a long period either… more just overwhelmed and tired sometimes.
